parallel_validity: Conceptually valid: both involve quality gates and preference parameters, but domains differ (UI code vs video). The analogy helps structure thinking, but direct translation requires domain-specific rules and dimensions.
lessons_from_impeccable: Define a comprehensive set of deterministic, measurable video quality rules (e.g., min resolution, max motion blur, exposure range, audio clarity) that are objective and computable.
Structure rules clearly so they can be automatically checked, reducing reliance on LLM for basic quality assessment.
Use rule composition: combine multiple detectors into a single quality score or pass/fail gate.
lessons_from_taste_skill: Replace binary accept/reject with continuous tunable dimensions (dials) for aesthetic aspects like mood, dynamism, composition, etc.
Allow users or contexts to adjust these dials, enabling personalized or scenario-specific taste models.
Use a small set of orthogonal parameters to keep the model interpretable and controllable.
detector_set_recommendation: Yes, formalize a set of deterministic video quality detectors akin to impeccable's 60 rules. This would provide a reliable, low-cost first-pass filter before LLM or human judgment, and can be continuously updated with new objective criteria.
preference_dials_recommendation: Yes, but start with a handful of well-defined dials (e.g., emotional intensity, visual dynamism, narrative coherence) learned from human ratings. Ensure dials are orthogonal and have clear semantic meaning to enable user control.
architecture: 1. Quality Gate: Run a deterministic detector set (e.g., 60 rules) on every video clip. Output a quality score or pass/fail. 2. If passed, feed clip into a preference model that outputs scores along tunable dials (e.g., mood, motion, density). 3. The wiki LLM uses these scores to rank or filter clips based on user-provided dial values or default settings. The LLM can also override or augment with semantic tags. The detectors are algorithmic; the preference model is either a learned scoring function or a rule-based combination of human judgments.
verdict: Adopting structured detectors and tunable preference dials from frontend skills can systematically improve video quality and taste assessment, but must be carefully adapted to the visual domain.
